chapter_seo_title: The Day Curfew – Gao Zhijian vs the Ma Family Warrior (Ch. 567)
chapter_meta_description: Gao Zhijian finds Li Sui lost in the curfew-dark streets. A cavalry charge, a melon-hammer duel, and a raw display of strength earn him a soldier’s offer.
og_title: A Bone-Crunching Night on the Curfew Streets
og_description: Gao Zhijian meets Li Sui, face-blocks a charging horse, and brawls with a military brute in this raw, muscle-driven chapter.
twitter_title: Gao Zhijian’s Big Fight: Melon Hammers, Horses, and a Lost Girl
twitter_description: Gao Zhijian catches a horse mid-charge, fights a melon-hammer warrior to a standstill, and rescues Li Huowang’s “daughter.” Pure muscle horror.

lore_anchors.definition: A lineage of martial power inherited from the ancient School of Military Strategy; not meant for common practice and requires special talent or bloodline.
A large, rounded metal hammer resembling a melon in shape, used as a heavy two-handed or paired weapon in Chinese martial tradition.
The fleshy web between thumb and index finger, a common pressure point and site of hand injury in wuxia and xianxia fight scenes.
An official lockdown imposed during the day or night, often signaling a supernatural hunt or ritual; violators may be killed on sight.
A military flare used to call reinforcements or alert authorities of a threat; in the Dao-Twisted World, it indicates organized supernatural response.
A title for the chief imperial adviser on religious and mystical matters; in this novel, a white-bearded old man who takes Li Huowang away on a flying sword.
A low-ranking officer position in the Ming-style military hierarchy, commanding a small unit of soldiers.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Who is Gao Zhijian and why is his strength so huge?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Gao Zhijian is a quiet, simple-minded member of Li Huowang’s group who trained in a forbidden military blood technique. His raw power is innate but unrefined, relying on brute force rather than formal martial arts.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is there a Day Curfew in the Upper Capital?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The novel does not fully explain it yet, but a “Day Curfew” in the Dao-Twisted World usually means the authorities are hunting a supernatural entity or preparing for a dangerous ritual that cannot be witnessed. Violators are killed on sight.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Who is Ma Wu and what is the Ma family?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Ma Wu is a towering warrior from the Ma family, a hereditary military clan. He respects strength and proper lineage—he challenges Gao Zhijian because he believes military arts should not be practiced by “unworthy” outsiders. After losing the exchange, he offers a position in the Ma family’s ranks.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Li Sui actually Li Huowang’s daughter?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Li Sui is the sentient Black Tai Sui parasite that lives inside Li Huowang, often called his “daughter.” She looks like a young girl and feels genuine attachment to him, but she is a supernatural entity, not a biological child.
